intro.heading: The training gets done. The thanks never happens.
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: A manager spends the first week of every month chasing training. Some carers finish the modules the day they are sent. Others need three reminders. The people who do it on time get no more than the people who do not, and the manager is too busy to say well done. A few of the best carers have started to ask why they bother. The manager wants a simple monthly scheme with a real reward, but does not want a spreadsheet of points, a leaderboard that embarrasses anyone, or a cheque that causes a payroll problem. Here is how the month goes.

trail.text: The manager sends the monthly training and a reminder.
Half the team finishes. The rest say they are busy.
A second reminder goes out. A few more finish.
Nobody has said thank you to the carers who did it first time.
One of the best carers asks why on time does not count for more.
Nobody. Any points are in someone's head, or a notebook.
A reward is promised, and then forgotten in the next busy week.
“How do you keep your staff motivated?” There is no record of anything.

trail_close: The training was never the problem. The gap is between the work people do and the recognition they get for it. Here is how CareStream turns that into a scheme you can run in a few minutes a month.

why.heading: Staff recognition works best when it is fair, visible and tied to real work

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: How does the employee incentive scheme work?
items.a: You set up one campaign for one calendar month. You choose which events earn points and how many, write the rewards and set a target. A care manager approves it, staff earn points as they finish training, and the people who reach the target claim the reward.

Five things: completing a training module, finishing it on or before its due date, completing a CPD course, completing an onboarding flow, and having a practical sign-off recorded. You pick which of them count and how many points each is worth.

items.q: The title says follow ups and audits. Do those earn points?
items.a: Not directly. Completing an audit does not earn points. Points come from training modules, and that includes an ad hoc module you allocate after a session or an incident. Retrying a wrong answer in the Follow-up tab does not earn points on its own. If you allocate a module as a follow up and a carer finishes it, that module counts like any other.

items.q: Could someone earn points just by clicking through?
items.a: No. A module with questions earns points only once the pass mark is reached. A failed assessment earns nothing, and a module that needs a practical earns nothing until a manager signs it off.

items.q: Who decides what reward people get?
items.a: You do. A reward is free text, with an optional photo, a points target and an optional limit on places. CareStream never buys vouchers or moves money. Cash and many gift cards can count as pay, so check with your payroll provider.

items.q: Will staff see how they compare with each other?
items.a: No. Each carer sees only their own points in My incentives. There is no leaderboard. Managers see the results on the campaign page and the Staff incentives card on the dashboard.

items.q: Why does a care manager have to approve it?
items.a: So that someone senior stands behind every reward. An admin builds the campaign, then a staff member whose job role is Care Manager or Registered Manager approves it and each reward claim. If nobody has that job role, the campaign cannot be submitted.

items.q: What does it cost to try, and which plan do I need?
items.a: Staff incentives are on the Professional and Enterprise plans. You can create a free account and try CareStream with a 14 day free trial, and the pricing page shows what each plan includes.

faqs.heading: Employee incentive schemes in care, answered

items.q: What is a staff incentive scheme in a care service?
items.a: It is a planned way of rewarding the behaviour you want, such as finishing training on time. In CareStream it runs for one month at a time, and points follow evidence that training was done. Our guide to staff incentive schemes goes into more detail.

items.q: What staff rewards can I offer?
items.a: Anything you choose to write in the reward box, with a photo if you like. Common ones are a voucher, an extra break or a small treat. CareStream does not buy or hand over rewards, so you do that yourself.

items.q: Does staff recognition have to cost money?
items.a: No. A reward can be a thank you from the owner, a named mention in a team meeting or a small treat in the staff room. The points simply give you a fair, visible way to decide who has earned it.
No. Everyone means all current staff, with agency staff left out. You can instead choose the individual people who take part.

items.q: What happens when a limited reward runs out?
items.a: The earliest person to reach the target gets it. People who miss out see a thank-you message that points them back to their training. If two people reach it at exactly the same moment, a care manager is asked to decide.

items.q: How do I get staff to finish training on time?
items.a: Make it worth their while and make it easy. A small monthly reward helps, and so does allocating short modules with a due date. There is more in our post on chasing training completions.

items.q: Is an incentive scheme something the CQC looks at?
items.a: The CQC does not ask for one. It does look at whether staff get the support and training they need. See CQC guidance on Regulation 18. A scheme that encourages people to finish training can help you show that training happens, but it is not a pass or a rating.

items.q: What does the law say about staff training?
items.a: Regulation 18 on staffing says staff must receive appropriate support, training, professional development, supervision and appraisal as is necessary to enable them to carry out their duties. It does not mention incentives, so how you encourage staff is up to you.

guide.heading: How to run a fair employee incentive scheme in care
guide.lede: A good scheme is small, clear and fair. People should know what earns a reward, believe the points are honest, and see the reward arrive. Everything else is decoration.

sections.h3: Start small and keep it honest
paragraphs: Pick one or two behaviours that matter this month, such as finishing the new training by its due date. Resist the urge to reward everything at once. Tell the team the rules in plain words before the month starts, and keep them the same until the month ends.

Make the reward worth the effort but not so large that people feel pressure to cut corners. Where a reward is paid through pay, check with your payroll provider first. Recognition also costs nothing: a named thank you in a team meeting often lands as well as a voucher.

checklist: Is there a staff member with the job role Care Manager or Registered Manager to approve it?
Have you picked the events that earn points, and the points for each?
Is the reward written down, with a target and a limit on places if you want one?
Does everyone know the rules, the month it runs and how to see their own points?

paragraphs: At the end of the month download the results and look at who finished and who did not. If the same people never reach the target, ask whether the training is too long or the due dates are unrealistic before you ask whether they care. Then change one thing and run the next month.

guide.note: For the inspector. The scheme is your own choice. What helps is the record underneath it: who was asked to complete training, who passed and when.
